key_insight: A pretrained image-editing model can act as a shared numerical-simulation interface when physical fields and parameters are encoded visually and learned through lightweight adapters.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a single vision-based model could emulate a wide range of solid mechanics and PDE solvers, from elasticity and fracture to transport and flow, with a unified training recipe.
method: Render states and solutions as images; inject scalar parameters via lightweight adapters.
Supervise the model with established numerical or analytic solvers across many PDEs and constitutive problems.
Use the same pretrained architecture for static, time-dependent, and shock-like dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful application to heterogeneous elliptic, evolution, flow, fracture, and transport problems, with a failed Kuramoto-Sivashinsky case highlighting a limit on chaotic long-horizon simulation.
watch_item: Image/latent representations make numerical range selection and enforcement of governing equations or invariants difficult, which can limit physical fidelity.
paper_title: Image Editing Models are Numerical Solvers
